issues.description: The template's Stock.findStockIngredient method has a different parameter list than described in the problem statement and implemented in the solution. The problem UML and the solution expect findStockIngredient(String) returning a StockIngredient, but the template defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean). Moreover, the template's add(...) and take(...) methods call findStockIngredient(String) (no boolean), creating an internal signature mismatch that will confuse students and cause compilation errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template Stock.java to provide findStockIngredient(String name) matching the UML and the solution (or add an overload that delegates to the case-sensitive/insensitive implementation). Ensure add(...) and take(...) call the same signature. This alignment will match the problem statement and allow students to compile and implement SealSaloon as intended.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Stock.findStockIngredient(String) but the template Stock class defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean caseSensitive). The solution implements findStockIngredient(String) (no boolean). This parameter/signature mismatch can confuse students: they will look for the single-argument method declared in the exercise specification but only find a different signature in the starter code, making it unclear which method to use or implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the specification: provide Stock.findStockIngredient(String name) (no boolean) in the template (either by replacing the two-argument method or adding an overloaded single-argument method). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to mention the caseSensitive parameter if that behavior is intended.
